## Intent
Hypothesis: Halide-generated parallel code for the expressible math walk can approach the streaming ceiling even when the RNG-order walk must remain scalar.

## Cache saturation
The L1d spill at N≈963 falls below the smallest measured point (N=4000), so L1d-resident behavior is never observed. From N=4000 to N=16000, ns/p drops from ~40 to ~32 across all death rates as fixed per-frame overhead amortizes — the prologue initializes ~8 stack structs via repeated `stp xzr, xzr`. The L2→DRAM spill at N≈61680 coincides with N=65000, where q=0.01 hits its best 28.911 ns/p; beyond this, cost rises mildly to ~30–31 ns/p, a ~6% knee. Death rate does not reshape the curve: q=0.25 tracks q=0.01 within noise (N=4M: 29.583 vs 31.428 ns/p), confirming the floor is scalar compute, not cache pressure.

## Bandwidth
Peak is 2.35 GB/s at N=65000, q=0.01 — 9.3% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling. The algo is compute/overhead-bound everywhere. Bandwidth rises from 1.7 GB/s (N=4000) to ~2.3 GB/s (N=65000) as overhead amortizes, then plateaus at 2.0–2.3 GB/s through N=4M. Death rate triggers no transition: q=0.25 sustains 2.0–2.3 GB/s identically to q=0.01, because the bottleneck is scalar byte-granular scatter, not streaming throughput.

## Assembly
Zero vector-suffixed instructions — no NEON whatsoever. The math walk is delegated to `_halide_b2_math` via `bl`; the step function is entirely scalar. The particle loop uses scalar `ldp s5, s6` / `ldr s17`, then `fadd s5`, `fmul s5`, `fsub s5`, `fcvtzs`. The scatter is byte-granular: `ldrb w2, [x1]`, `add w2, w2, w12`, `cmp w2, #0xff`, `csel w2, w2, w11, lo`, `strb w2, [x1]` — repeated per channel plus `strb w11, [x3, x0]` for alpha. RNG uses scalar `eor`/`ror`/`clz`. This byte-store scatter with per-channel clamping caps bandwidth at 9% of ceiling and explains the total absence of vectorization: the non-Halide-expressible walks dominate.

## Verdict
Refuted — the algo never exceeds 2.35 GB/s (9.3% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling) and the step function contains zero vector instructions. The Halide math call is overshadowed by scalar RNG (`eor`/`ror`/`clz`) and byte-granular scatter (`ldrb`/`strb` with `cmp #0xff`/`csel` per channel). Death rate is irrelevant: q=0.25 matches q=0.01, confirming the bottleneck is scalar compute structure, not churn or bandwidth.
